content.text: I will first join the `Musical_Preferences` and `Musical_Styles` tables to link musical styles with customer preferences. Then, I will count the occurrences of each style as a 1st, 2nd, or 3rd preference, grouping the results by style name to present a consolidated view in a single row per style.

args.sql:
SELECT
    T2.StyleName,
    SUM(CASE WHEN T1.PreferenceSeq = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS "1st Preference",
    SUM(CASE WHEN T1.PreferenceSeq = 2 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS "2nd Preference",
    SUM(CASE WHEN T1.PreferenceSeq = 3 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS "3rd Preference"
FROM "entertainmentagency.main.Musical_Preferences" AS T1
INNER JOIN "entertainmentagency.main.Musical_Styles" AS T2
  ON T1.StyleID = T2.StyleID
WHERE
  T1.PreferenceSeq IN (1, 2, 3)
GROUP BY
  T2.StyleName
ORDER BY
  T2.StyleName
